Description: A chronic autoimmune skin condition that causes rapid buildup of skin cells, resulting in scaling and red itchy patches.
Causes: Immune system dysfunction; genetics; stress; infections; cold weather
Precautions: Keep skin moisturized; avoid triggers like stress and alcohol; use prescribed creams; avoid scratching

Description: Enlarged, twisted veins usually appearing in the legs, caused by weakened or damaged vein valves.
Causes: Prolonged standing; obesity; pregnancy; age; family history
Precautions: Elevate legs when resting; wear compression stockings; exercise regularly; avoid standing for long periods

Description: A bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi that spreads through contaminated food and water.
Causes: Contaminated food or water; poor sanitation; close contact with an infected person
Precautions: Drink boiled or bottled water; maintain hygiene; get vaccinated; avoid street food

Description: A highly contagious viral infection caused by the varicella-zoster virus that leads to itchy, blister-like rash.
Causes: Varicella-zoster virus; close contact with an infected person
Precautions: Isolate from others; avoid scratching; trim nails; take prescribed antiviral medicines

Description: A common and highly contagious skin infection that mainly affects infants and children, caused by bacteria.
Causes: Staphylococcus or Streptococcus bacteria; skin cuts; poor hygiene
Precautions: Keep wounds clean and covered; avoid sharing towels; wash hands frequently; use prescribed antibiotics

Description: A mosquito-borne viral infection causing high fever, severe joint pain and rash, transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes.
Causes: Aedes mosquito bite; stagnant water breeding grounds
Precautions: Use mosquito repellents; remove stagnant water; stay hydrated; avoid aspirin/ibuprofen for fever

Description: A skin infection caused by fungi that thrive in warm and moist areas of the body.
Causes: Excess moisture; poor hygiene; tight clothing; weakened immunity
Precautions: Keep skin dry and clean; wear breathable cotton clothes; avoid sharing personal items; use antifungal cream

Description: A mild viral infection of the nose and throat, usually harmless and self-limiting.
Causes: Rhinovirus infection; cold weather; weakened immunity
Precautions: Rest well; stay hydrated; wash hands frequently; avoid close contact with sick people

Description: An infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid.
Causes: Bacterial, viral or fungal infection; smoking; weakened immune system
Precautions: Get vaccinated; avoid smoking; practice good hygiene; rest and stay hydrated

Description: Swollen veins in the lower rectum or anus, causing pain, itching and bleeding, occurring internally and externally.
Causes: Straining during bowel movements; chronic constipation; pregnancy; obesity
Precautions: Eat a high fiber diet; stay hydrated; avoid straining; exercise regularly

Description: Inflammation of one or more joints, causing pain, swelling and reduced range of motion.
Causes: Autoimmune disorders; joint wear and tear; infections; age
Precautions: Maintain healthy weight; exercise gently; apply heat or cold packs; take prescribed anti-inflammatory medicine

Description: A skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become clogged with oil and dead skin cells.
Causes: Excess oil production; hormonal changes; bacteria; diet
Precautions: Wash face gently twice daily; avoid touching face; avoid oily cosmetics; eat a balanced diet

Description: A chronic condition in which airways narrow, swell and produce extra mucus, causing breathing difficulty.
Causes: Allergens; air pollution; respiratory infections; genetics
Precautions: Avoid known triggers; use prescribed inhalers; avoid smoking; monitor breathing regularly

Description: A condition in which the force of blood against artery walls is consistently too high.
Causes: Unhealthy diet; obesity; lack of exercise; stress; genetics
Precautions: Reduce salt intake; exercise regularly; manage stress; monitor blood pressure regularly

Description: A neurological condition causing intense, throbbing headaches, often with nausea and light sensitivity.
Causes: Hormonal changes; stress; certain foods; lack of sleep
Precautions: Identify and avoid triggers; maintain a regular sleep schedule; stay hydrated; manage stress

Description: Age-related wear and tear affecting the spinal disks in the neck, leading to pain and stiffness.
Causes: Age-related degeneration; poor posture; previous neck injury
Precautions: Maintain good posture; do neck stretching exercises; avoid heavy lifting; use ergonomic furniture

Description: A condition marked by yellowing of the skin and eyes due to high bilirubin levels, often linked to liver issues.
Causes: Liver disease; bile duct obstruction; certain infections
Precautions: Avoid alcohol; eat a liver-friendly diet; stay hydrated; get adequate rest

Description: A mosquito-borne disease caused by Plasmodium parasites, transmitted through Anopheles mosquito bites.
Causes: Anopheles mosquito bite; travel to endemic regions
Precautions: Use mosquito nets and repellents; eliminate standing water; take preventive medication when traveling

Description: An infection in any part of the urinary system, most commonly the bladder and urethra.
Causes: Bacterial infection; poor hygiene; dehydration; holding urine too long
Precautions: Drink plenty of water; urinate frequently; maintain genital hygiene; avoid holding urine

Description: An immune system reaction to a substance that is usually harmless, such as pollen or certain foods.
Causes: Pollen; dust mites; certain foods; pet dander; medications
Precautions: Avoid known allergens; keep living areas clean; use air purifiers; carry prescribed antihistamines

Description: A digestive disorder in which stomach acid frequently flows back into the esophagus, causing irritation.
Causes: Weak lower esophageal sphincter; obesity; spicy or fatty foods; smoking
Precautions: Avoid large meals before bedtime; reduce spicy and fatty foods; maintain healthy weight; avoid smoking

Description: An adverse and unexpected reaction of the body to a medication.
Causes: Allergic reaction to medication; drug interactions; individual sensitivity
Precautions: Inform doctors of known allergies; avoid self-medication; read medicine labels carefully; seek immediate care if severe

Description: Open sores that develop on the inner lining of the stomach or upper small intestine.
Causes: H. pylori infection; long-term use of NSAIDs; excess acid production; smoking
Precautions: Avoid NSAIDs and spicy food; eat smaller frequent meals; avoid smoking and alcohol; manage stress

Description: A chronic condition that affects how the body turns food into energy due to insulin issues.
Causes: Insulin resistance; genetics; obesity; sedentary lifestyle
Precautions: Maintain a balanced diet; exercise regularly; monitor blood sugar levels; take prescribed medication
